The two-cause diagnosis is real, not rhetorical. critiques.concern: The bare-subject fallback mislabels ordinary scientific-codebase commits as lifecycle transitions, and reports the resulting wrong timestamps as `Exact` — the proposal's own named worst-case regression, in a default-on module, for the postdoc adopter the standing directive prioritizes. When a subject carries no `dev/proposals:` / `dev/plans:` prefix, `_stage_for_subject` sets `phrase = body` and searches `review` / `response` / `revise` across the ENTIRE subject, and tests `^open` / `^decision` against the entire subject. I ran 8 realistic hydrogeology-codebase subjects through the proposed classifier this session; all 8 misclassify: "Add response surface model for aquifer recharge" → `revised`; "Add impulse response function to the transport solver" → `revised`; "fix: revise the calibration constants for Darcy flux" → `revised`; "literature review of contaminant transport models" → `reviewed`; "open sourcing the transport module" → `open`; "Decision tree classifier for facies prediction" → `decision`; "revise mesh resolution near the well screen" → `revised`; "review: tighten the recharge bounds" → `reviewed`. ("docs: address reviewer comments" and a merge-branch subject correctly return `None`.) Exposure is limited to commits that touch a proposal file — but that is exactly the adopter's mixed "update the model and amend the proposal" commit, and Cairn's own corpus proves non-lifecycle commits do touch proposal files: `check_cairn: resolve dev/ self-host claim-path findings (implements 2026-06-12 proposal)` is one of the 73. The proposal defers this entirely to a post-hoc tripwire under *Signals the change is wrong* instead of measuring it before the Decision.

The measured trade is cheap: requiring the `dev/<tree>:` prefix costs exactly one tier on Cairn's corpus (`ast-known-new-repin` Exact→Good, driven by one unprefixed `Append Gemini … Review` subject) and eliminates all 8 adopter false positives. Either (a) adopt prefix-required and add the unprefixed `Append/Refine Gemini … Review of <stem> proposal` shape as a narrow, explicitly-listed second accepted form so Cairn keeps 11 Exact without opening the general bare fallback, or (b) keep the bare fallback and record in the proposal that it is a deliberate precision-for-recall trade, with the measured adopter false-positive set above quoted as the known cost. Add the 8 adopter subjects to the frozen corpus test with their intended classifications either way.

critiques.concern: The `sharpening` exclusion is NOT "carried over … unchanged" — it silently widens from a head-anchored special case into a whole-phrase suppressor, creating a new false-negative class that the proposed tests would not catch. The proposal states: "The `sharpening` exclusion is carried over from the current `reviewed` pattern unchanged — it is not part of this defect." Measured, that is false. The shipped pattern is `^Review\b(?!.*\bsharpening\b)` — anchored, so the lookahead is only ever reachable for a subject literally beginning with "Review". The proposed pattern is `(?<!-)\breview\b(?!-)(?!.*\bsharpening\b)` applied via `.search()` over the whole stage phrase, so ANY subject containing "sharpening" anywhere after a `review` token is now suppressed. Demonstrated this session: `dev/proposals: foo -- Internal review (fresh-context panel)` → `reviewed`, but the near-identical `dev/proposals: foo -- Internal review (fresh-context panel) + Sharpening` → `None`, and `Append Gemini External Review of foo proposal (sharpening round)` → `None`. This is not an exotic token: 42 commits in Cairn's history carry "sharpen" in the subject, including three plan-review commits of exactly the vulnerable shape (`8606203`, `51f2c10`, `28816f0`, all `dev/plans: <slug> -- Plan review (fresh-context Internal) + Sharpening`). Live impact today is zero — none of the 42 touches `dev/proposals/` in the last 400 commits — but the vocabulary is in active use, so one proposal-side "Internal review … + Sharpening" subject silently drops the `reviewed` stage and downgrades the row to `Good` with no signal. Proposed test #3 asserts only `"Review sharpening pass"` → unclassified, which passes for the wrong reason and manufactures false confidence that the exclusion is unchanged.
critiques.grounding: Compared `templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/gitmeta.py:24` (shipped `^Review\b(?!.*\bsharpening\b)`) against the proposal's `reviewed` pattern, both exec'd and run this session. Ran the paired subjects above through each. Counted the exposure with `git log --format="%s" | grep -ci sharpen` → 42, then iterated the last 400 commits checking `git show --stat` for `dev/proposals/` on each sharpening-subject commit → zero hits today.
critiques.suggested_fix: Stop describing this as a no-op and decide it explicitly. Either scope the exclusion to the head-anchored form it actually had (e.g. apply it only when `review` leads the phrase), or drop it and state the intended behaviour. Whichever is chosen, add two tests pinning BOTH directions: `dev/proposals: <stem> -- Internal review (fresh-context panel) + Sharpening` → `reviewed` (the false-negative guard), and an implementation-style `Phase 2 (A) review Sharpening: harden facade loader` → `None` (the suppression the exclusion is presumably for). Correct the sentence in P1 so it no longer claims the exclusion is unchanged.

critiques.concern: The repair makes `days_*` and `hours_*` openly contradict each other on 4 of 12 rows under an `Exact` label — and the proposal names that exact shape as the signal the change is WRONG, which makes its own tripwire unusable and would lead an implementer to revert a correct fix. *Signals the change is wrong* says: "a proposal reports `Exact` while an `hours_*` value contradicts the header dates in the same row. That would mean a subject matched the wrong stage — the one regression that is worse than the defect." Measured post-fix, four rows ship exactly that shape: `adopter-licensing-compliance`, `first-session-survivability`, `record-corrections`, and `solo-legacy-adopter-path` each carry `days_revised_to_decision = 11` (from header dates) alongside `hours_revised_to_decision ≈ 116.46` hours = 4.85 days (from commit timestamps), tier `Exact`. The cause is NOT misclassification — I checked the resolved SHAs and the classifier is right; the header `**Date opened**` is `2026-07-11` while the actual open commit `adaa9b5` is `2026-07-17T11:55:42-04:00`, i.e. the header dates are backdated by six days. So the tripwire fires immediately on Cairn's own corpus for a reason the proposal never anticipated. This also matters on its own terms: before the fix every `hours_*` was empty so the divergence was invisible; after the fix a third of the rows visibly disagree with themselves, and the first adopter's first read of the repaired tool shows "11 days" and "4.85 days" side by side in one row marked `Exact`.
critiques.grounding: Ran `proposal_rows(Path('/Users/kendal30/Code/cairn'))` through the real `tools/_lifecycle_metrics/extract.py` with the proposed classifier patched into `extract._resolve_stage_commits`, printing `days_*` and `hours_*` side by side and flagging any row where both are non-empty and disagree by more than one day: 4 hits, all `days_revised_to_decision` = 11 vs `hours_revised_to_decision` ≈ 116.46, all tier `Exact`. Cross-checked against a per-proposal dump of the resolved `(sha, timestamp, subject)` per stage, which confirmed every assignment is semantically correct and the divergence traces to backdated `**Date opened**` headers.
critiques.suggested_fix: Rewrite the first bullet of *Signals the change is wrong* so it distinguishes backdated-header divergence (expected, benign, present on 4/12 rows today) from stage misclassification (the real regression) — e.g. key the signal on a NEGATIVE `hours_*`, or on an `hours_*` that disagrees with `days_*` in the opposite direction from the header/commit gap. Then add the four rows above to the corpus test as an explicitly expected divergence with the six-day header/commit gap named, so a future implementer does not read it as breakage. Consider noting the divergence in the P3 docstring alongside the degradation-cause correction.

critiques.concern: Plan-lifecycle review vocabulary classifies as proposal `reviewed`, which the proposal's own argument for accepting the `plans?` prefix makes a live conflation rather than a theoretical one. P1 argues that accepting the `plans?` prefix is "required, not cosmetic: plan-open and plan-archive commits move the proposal file and therefore appear in its `git log --follow` history." That is true — and it is also why plan-STAGE subjects now compete for proposal-stage slots. Measured over the last 60 commits: `eab7141 dev/plans: first-session-survivability -- Code review (fresh-context, disclosed scribe)` → `reviewed` and `224c928 dev/plans: adopter-licensing-compliance -- Code review (fresh-context, not implementer)` → `reviewed`. Neither touches a proposal file today so there is no live corruption, but the classifier draws no distinction between a plan's Code review and a proposal's Review. Likewise `dev/plans: open <slug> (+ archive proposal)` → `open`, which IS in the corpus and IS harmless only because the proposal's own open commit always precedes it chronologically and first-match-wins. The compound risk is concrete: if the genuine proposal review commit were ever suppressed (see the `Sharpening` finding above) and a later plan Code-review commit touched the proposal file, the `reviewed` slot would be filled with a post-Decision timestamp and produce a negative `hours_reviewed_to_revised`.
critiques.grounding: Swept the proposed classifier over `git log -60 --format='%h%x00%s'` this session: 6 `open`, 6 `decision`, 12 `revised`, 17 `reviewed`, 19 `None`. `eab7141` and `224c928` classify `reviewed`; `1ebafb1` and `57d1daf` (`dev/plans: open … (+ archive proposal)`) classify `open`. Cross-checked against the 75-subject `--follow` corpus: the two Code-review commits are absent from it, so exposure is latent, not live.
critiques.suggested_fix: Either exclude the `plans?` branch from the `reviewed` / `revised` stages (keep it only for `open`, which is the case P1 actually justifies), or state explicitly in the scope fence that plan-stage and proposal-stage vocabulary are deliberately conflated and that correctness rests on first-match-wins chronological ordering. Add `dev/plans: <slug> -- Code review (fresh-context, disclosed scribe)` to the frozen corpus test with whichever classification is intended, so the choice is pinned rather than incidental.

critiques.concern: The de-anchored figure is 52, not the claimed 51, and Alternative 3 as literally worded produces 0, not 51. Two small precision problems in the same argument. First: re-measuring on the exact 73-subject set as of `7d2d034`, stripping the leading `^` from all four shipped patterns and matching with `.search()`, I get **52/73**, not the stated 51/73. Second, and more confusing for a reader: *Cause 1* correctly states that switching `.match()` to `.search()` alone "would change nothing" because the `^` lives inside the pattern string — but Alternative 3 is worded as "Just remove the `^` anchors", and removing the anchors while keeping the shipped `pattern.match(subject)` call at `templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/gitmeta.py:83` yields **0/73**, not 51. The 51 (52) figure silently requires BOTH changes. Neither error touches the argument's conclusion — 15 of the 52 are slug-driven false positives, exactly as claimed, and de-anchoring really does convert a total miss into a large false-positive rate — but this repository's verify-before-asserting discipline makes a stated measured count worth getting right.
critiques.grounding: Reconstructed the 73-subject set as of `7d2d034` by removing from the 75-subject HEAD corpus the two subjects added by `cc66d2b` and `33edd10`. Then ran three variants over it this session: shipped patterns with `.match()` → 0/73 (confirms the proposal's headline); shipped patterns de-anchored but still `.match()` → 0/73; shipped patterns de-anchored with `.search()` → 52/73. Proposed classifier over the same set → 68/73 with exactly 5 unclassified, matching the proposal precisely.
critiques.suggested_fix: Correct 51 → 52 in both the *Why it misses* section and Alternative 3, and reword Alternative 3 to "remove the `^` anchors and switch `.match()` to `.search()`" so the measurement is reproducible from the description. Optionally note that de-anchoring alone (keeping `.match()`) still yields 0/73, which strengthens rather than weakens Cause 1.

critiques.concern: P2's fall-through removal changes nothing on the real corpus, so "This is not hypothetical" overstates its evidentiary basis. The proposal introduces P2 with "This is not hypothetical" and cites the two `open`-classified commits in `review-record-integrity`'s history. I tested the actual differential: running the shipped fall-through loop shape (`gitmeta.py:81-85`, which re-tests a subject against remaining stages when its correct slot is already filled) against the proposed loop, BOTH driven by the new P1 patterns, across all 12 proposals — the resolved slot assignments are identical for **0 of 12**. The proposal does concede this honestly two sentences later ("P1's hyphen guard blocks that particular subject, but the fall-through is the general hazard"), so this is a framing issue rather than a false claim. But an opening "This is not hypothetical" attached to a change with zero measured effect on the corpus invites a reviewer to over-credit it, and P2 ends up pinned only by the synthetic proposed test #5.
critiques.grounding: Implemented both loop shapes this session over `gitmeta._git_log_for_path` output for all 12 proposal files, with the proposed patterns held constant, and diffed the resulting `{open, reviewed, revised, decision}` SHA assignments per proposal. Result: 0/12 differ. Confirmed the specific cited case: `dev/plans: open review-record-integrity (+ archive proposal)` classifies `open` under the new patterns, and under the old loop its fall-through re-test yields no match for `decision`/`revised`/`reviewed` because the hyphen guard blocks `review-record`.
critiques.suggested_fix: Keep P2 — it is cheap, correct, and makes classification a pure function of the subject, which is the right invariant. But retitle the justification honestly: say the fall-through is a latent defect of the same mechanism with no currently-observable effect (measured 0/12), rather than "not hypothetical". Keep proposed test #5 and note in the test docstring that it is the only thing pinning P2, since the live corpus does not exercise it.

critiques.concern: The `0 Best-effort` headline is not reproducible under concurrent git load, which the implementing plan's verification step should account for. While the full pytest suite was running in the background, an otherwise identical pipeline run returned `2026-07-11-claude-record-corrections` as `Best-effort` — {'Exact': 10, 'Good': 1, 'Best-effort': 1} instead of the stable {'Exact': 11, 'Good': 1}. Three subsequent runs on a quiet tree were stable at 11/1/0. The cause is pre-existing and NOT introduced by this proposal: `_git_log_for_path` returns `[]` on any non-zero git exit (`templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/gitmeta.py:50-51`), so transient git contention silently degrades a whole row to `Best-effort` with no signal. This is genuinely outside the proposal's stated scope and I am not asking it to be fixed here. But it bears on two things the proposal does assert: the `0 Best-effort` smoke check under *Examples / smoke checks* can fail spuriously, and proposed test #6 (synthetic repo, end-to-end, asserting `stage_timestamp_reliability == 'Exact'`) is exposed to the same flakiness inside a parallel test run.
critiques.grounding: Observed directly this session: one `proposal_rows` run issued while `~/conda_envs/lhm/bin/python -m pytest bootstrap/tests` was executing in the background returned `record-corrections` at `Best-effort`; three re-runs after the suite finished (1437 passed, 123.55s) returned {'Exact': 11, 'Good': 1} identically. Traced to the unconditional `return []` on `result.returncode != 0` at `templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/gitmeta.py:50-51`.
critiques.suggested_fix: Add one line to *Examples / smoke checks* noting that the `0 Best-effort` verification must be run on a quiet tree (no concurrent git operations), since a transient git failure degrades a row silently. For proposed test #6, use an isolated `tmp_path` repo (which it already specifies) and avoid asserting the tier on the live Cairn corpus inside the suite. Optionally route the underlying silent-degradation behaviour to the Maintainer as a separate observation — it is a pre-existing defect, not this proposal's, and should not expand this scope.

panel_raw.second_round:
RECOMMEND: revise, then accept — do not send this back to the drawing board. The diagnosis is correct, the fix is correct on Cairn's own corpus (I verified every one of the 48 slot assignments across 12 proposals by hand), the scope fence holds, and the citation discipline is unusually clean. Nothing I found undermines the central case that the shipped vocabulary reads nothing and should be repaired now.

One item genuinely gates the Decision: finding 1 (the bare-subject fallback). It is blocking not because the proposal is wrong but because it defers a decision that should be made with numbers in hand, and I now have the numbers. Under the standing postdoc-ready-first directive, shipping a default-on tool that labels "Add impulse response function to the transport solver" as a `revised` transition and reports the resulting timestamp as `Exact` is a genuine regression in the adopter path — before the fix that adopter got nothing, after it they get something wrong with a confidence label attached. The proposal itself names this as the one failure mode worse than the defect, then routes it to a post-hoc tripwire. The measured trade is cheap enough to settle in one revision round: requiring the `dev/<tree>:` prefix costs exactly one tier on Cairn's corpus (ast-known-new-repin Exact→Good, driven by a single unprefixed `Append Gemini … Review` subject) and takes all 8 adopter false positives to `None`. My suggested landing is the hybrid — prefix-required plus an explicitly-enumerated `Append/Refine … Review of <stem> proposal` form — which preserves 11 Exact AND closes the general fallback. Whichever way the Maintainer goes, it should be recorded as a deliberate precision/recall trade in the proposal body, not left to a recovery bullet.

Findings 2 and 3 are substantive but resolvable by appending a Response and a Revised section; neither requires re-measuring anything. Finding 2 is a corrected factual claim plus two tests. Finding 3 is a rewritten tripwire plus an expected-divergence assertion — and it matters disproportionately because as written the tripwire fires immediately on the shipped corpus, so an implementer following the proposal faithfully would revert a correct fix. Findings 4-7 are minor and can be folded into the same Response: correct 51→52, reword Alternative 3 so it is reproducible, soften "not hypothetical" on P2, decide the plan-vocabulary conflation, and add the quiet-tree caveat to the smoke checks.

On the two open questions I can speak to: the 41-entry lockfile staleness is correctly routed out — I confirmed it is real, pre-existing, caused by 501efe3, and that bumping 1 of 41 would make the record less coherent; bundling it here would be a scope breach. P3 should ride along: I confirmed the `__init__.py` twins are byte-identical (c0e169e7…) so the parity cost is one mechanical copy, and the sentence really is false in every clause of its cause list — leaving it while fixing the behaviour it mis-describes would be the worse outcome. I would also suggest P3 pick up one clause noting the days_*/hours_* divergence from finding 3, since the docstring is the only adopter-facing documentation of this tier.

For the second-round reviewer: the highest-value unchecked surface is the frozen corpus list in `bootstrap/tests/test_lifecycle_stage_patterns.py` once written. My findings 1, 2 and 4 each propose additions to it, and a frozen list assembled without them would lock in exactly the blind spots this review found. Second priority is re-verifying the transition-lint obligation section against that proposal's actual Revised text, which I read only as quoted here.

This is a genuinely well-disciplined defect proposal and most of its load-bearing claims survive independent verification. I reproduced the headline defect exactly: `proposal_rows(Path('.'))` at HEAD `cc66d2b` returns `Counter({'Best-effort': 12})`, and running the four shipped `_STAGE_COMMIT_PATTERNS` (`templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/gitmeta.py:17-25`) over the union of `git log --follow` subjects for all 12 proposal files gives 0 matches. Zero, not low. The diagnosis of two independent causes is right, and the refusal to "just drop the `^`" is correct on measurement.

I reproduced the post-fix result too: monkeypatching the proposal's exact `_stage_for_subject` into the live extractor yields `Counter({'Exact': 11, 'Good': 1})` — the claimed table, verbatim, at a HEAD two commits later than the one cited. That is a real repair with a real measured outcome.

The scope fence is the strongest part. It is explicit, enumerated, and — with one exception (critique 1) — honest. `PROPOSAL_COLUMNS` untouched, no config key, no CLI flag, no export, no second consumer, no doctrine edit, no commit-message convention. `bootstrap/scaffold.py --manifest` emits `dst\tsrc\tverbatim` with no hash, so the manifest row provably cannot move. The proposal even declines the two obvious capability temptations (configurable patterns, shared library with the sibling lint) and records them as rejected alternatives rather than leaving them implicit. Under "fix defects, build nothing new," the diff is one private classifier plus one test file, and the author resisted the pull toward generality.

Parity handling is correct and better-evidenced than most. Both twin pairs are byte-identical today (`gitmeta.py` = `5a47849b…` on both sides; `__init__.py` = `c0e169e7…` on both sides), and `bootstrap/tests/test_notice_install.py:98` is exactly the test claimed — it pairs every self-hosted twin from the manifest and asserts equal bytes, so editing one side reds the suite. Declining to bundle that is the right stopping-rule call, and routing it as an open question rather than silently fixing it is exactly the discipline this repo asks for.

The AST claim is precise, not reflexive, and demonstrably so: `bootstrap/tests/test_ast_attest.py:19` pins `_SCAFFOLD = _REPO / "bootstrap" / "_scaffold" / "__init__.py"` and verification runs over `sorted(_SCAFFOLD.parent.glob("*.py"))`. `gitmeta.py` lives under `templates/modules/default-on/` and cannot enter that glob. Citation accuracy is unusually high. critiques.concern: The `plans?` branch of `_STAGE_SCOPE_PREFIX_RE` breaches the proposal's own scope fence and, in the measured corpus, produces exclusively wrong classifications while changing no outcome. The fence states: "Tokens Cairn's log happens to contain but doctrine does not name — `archive`, `supersede`, `sharpening`, `claim-marker maintenance` — get **no** stage and are left unclassified." But stripping a `dev/plans: ` prefix makes plan-lifecycle commits classifiable, and every one that results is semantically inverted.
critiques.grounding: I ran the proposal's exact classifier over the 75 distinct `git log --follow` subjects for all 12 proposal files at HEAD `cc66d2b`, then ablated the `plans?` alternation. Exactly four subjects change classification, all `open` -> `None`: `dev/plans: open adopter-entry-doc-refresh; archive the accepted proposal`, `dev/plans: open adopter-licensing-compliance (+ archive proposal)`, `dev/plans: open first-session-survivability (+ archive proposal)`, `dev/plans: open review-record-integrity (+ archive proposal)`. Those are the proposal's ARCHIVE event, not its opening — `doctrine/proposals.md:69` says "Commit on **opening** a proposal (status `proposed`)." and `doctrine/proposals.md:78` says the "subsequent plan-open or trivial-implementing commit moves" an accepted proposal. So all four are the wrong end of the lifecycle. I then re-ran the full extractor with `plans?` removed from the prefix: `Counter({'Exact': 11, 'Good': 1})` — byte-identical to the with-`plans?` result. The branch buys nothing measured. It is harmless today only because first-match-wins fills `open` from the genuinely earlier open commit; a proposal whose own opening subject fails to classify (an adopter's tree, or any non-conforming Cairn subject) would take its `open` timestamp from the plan-open/archive commit and report it as `Exact` — precisely the regression the proposal itself names as worse than the defect ("A subject matches the wrong stage -> a wrong hour-delta, reported as `Exact`."). The proposal's stated justification inverts the inference: "Accepting the `plans?` prefix is required, not cosmetic: plan-open and plan-archive commits move the proposal file and therefore appear in its `git log --follow` history." That premise is true and is an argument for *recognising and rejecting* those subjects, not for stripping their prefix so they classify.
critiques.suggested_fix: Drop `plans?` from `_STAGE_SCOPE_PREFIX_RE` (making it `^(?:dev/)?proposals?\s*:\s*`), or add an explicit early return of `None` for a `dev/plans:`-prefixed subject. Add all six `dev/plans:` subjects in the corpus to the frozen regression list with expected `None`. Then delete the justification sentence, since the ablation shows the branch is not required. If the author believes plan-lifecycle recognition is wanted, that is new capability and must be routed to the Maintainer, not folded into a defect fix.

critiques.concern: One of the two cases offered as "Measured necessity" for the hyphen guard does not hold, and the test specified to pin the guard is non-discriminating as written.
critiques.grounding: The proposal asserts: "**Never match inside a hyphen compound** (`(?<!-)…(?!-)`). Measured necessity: without it, `dev/plans: archive review-record-integrity (Chunk C pointer + lifecycle close)` classifies as `reviewed`, and `Security-Review` inside an `open` subject does the same." I ablated the guard from both the `revised` and `reviewed` patterns and re-ran over all 75 corpus subjects. Exactly ONE subject flips: the `dev/plans: archive review-record-integrity …` one. `dev/proposals: open interpreter-trust-root-fallback (F2 split; Security-Review gated)` classifies as `open` with the guard and `open` without it — because `open` is head-anchored and first in `_STAGE_COMMIT_PATTERNS`' priority order, so the `reviewed` pattern is never evaluated for that subject. The second measured claim is false for the proposed design. The consequence reaches the test plan: Tests-required item 2 specifies asserting `dev/proposals: open interpreter-trust-root-fallback (F2 split; Security-Review gated)` -> `open`, which passes identically against an unguarded pattern. It is presented as pinning the hyphen guard and does not pin it. This is the failure mode the standing lesson "DO NOT CLAIM WHAT A TEST DOES WITHOUT READING IT" names, arriving one step early — a test asserted to discriminate before it exists.
critiques.suggested_fix: Correct the sentence to name the single measured case. Keep `dev/plans: archive review-record-integrity (Chunk C pointer + lifecycle close)` -> `None` as the guard's discriminating test (it is the only one in the corpus), and add a stage-phrase-position case such as `dev/proposals: interpreter-trust-root -- add Security-Review section` -> `None` so the guard is pinned where the `reviewed` pattern is actually reached. Keep the `Security-Review gated` case in the suite as a priority-order test, but label it as such rather than as guard evidence.

critiques.concern: The Rationale's transparency/reproducibility claim over-reads the post-fix numbers. Most of the newly-populated hour deltas measure commit batching latency, not deliberation elapsed time, and three are exactly zero — a reader will take `0.0` as a claim about review turnaround.
critiques.grounding: The proposal claims: "It also restores the sub-day resolution the tiers were designed around: post-fix, 11 of 12 proposals reach `Exact` and hour-level deltas populate." I ran the full post-fix simulation at HEAD `cc66d2b` and printed every delta. `hours_reviewed_to_revised` is exactly `0.0` for three proposals — `2026-07-22-claude-interpreter-trust-root-fallback`, `2026-07-22-claude-lockfile-provenance-fields`, `2026-07-22-claude-transition-lint`. Root cause verified in git: for interpreter-trust-root, `4f5f019` (`… -- Internal review (tailored fresh-context panel) + in-tree source`) and `841f17b` (`… -- Response + Revised (status: revised)`) both carry committer timestamp `2026-07-22T09:21:25-04:00`. Five of twelve rows also show `hours_open_to_reviewed` under 0.024 h (~85 s). These are honest readings of the commit record — the tool measures commits and now measures them correctly — but the CSV column will read `0.0` next to `Exact`, and Cairn's whole pitch is that its recorded deliberation is measurable. Shipping a default-on metric whose `Exact` tier frequently reports sub-second review->response gaps invites a reader (or the first external adopter) to conclude either that review is instantaneous or that the tool is broken again.
critiques.suggested_fix: Replace the Rationale sentence with one that says what the numbers measure: the interval between the commits that recorded each transition, which for batch-committed sessions can be near zero. Then pin the semantics rather than leaving them to be rediscovered — add at least one `0.0`-delta row (e.g. the interpreter-trust-root reviewed->revised pair) to the frozen corpus regression test with its expected value, so a future reader finds the case documented as intended behaviour rather than as a suspected defect.

numbered_critiques.grounding: Ablation over the 75 distinct `--follow` subjects at HEAD `cc66d2b`: exactly four subjects change classification, all `open` → `None` — `dev/plans: open adopter-entry-doc-refresh; archive the accepted proposal`, `dev/plans: open adopter-licensing-compliance (+ archive proposal)`, `dev/plans: open first-session-survivability (+ archive proposal)`, `dev/plans: open review-record-integrity (+ archive proposal)`. Those are the proposal's ARCHIVE event, not its opening — `doctrine/proposals.md:69` says "Commit on **opening** a proposal (status `proposed`)." and `:78` says the "subsequent plan-open or trivial-implementing commit moves" an accepted proposal. So all four are the wrong end of the lifecycle. Re-running the full extractor with `plans?` removed gives `Counter({'Exact': 11, 'Good': 1})` — byte-identical to the with-`plans?` result; the branch buys nothing measured, and is harmless today only because first-match-wins fills `open` from the genuinely earlier open commit. Separately, sweeping the proposed classifier over `git log -60` (6 `open`, 6 `decision`, 12 `revised`, 17 `reviewed`, 19 `None`): `eab7141 dev/plans: first-session-survivability -- Code review (fresh-context, disclosed scribe)` → `reviewed` and `224c928 dev/plans: adopter-licensing-compliance -- Code review (fresh-context, not implementer)` → `reviewed`. Neither is in the 75-subject `--follow` corpus, so exposure is latent, not live — but the classifier draws no distinction between a plan's Code review and a proposal's Review. The compound risk is concrete: if the genuine proposal review commit were ever suppressed (see R4) and a later plan Code-review commit touched the proposal file, the `reviewed` slot would take a post-Decision timestamp and produce a negative `hours_reviewed_to_revised`. A proposal whose own opening subject fails to classify (an adopter tree, or any non-conforming Cairn subject) would take its `open` timestamp from the plan-open/archive commit and report it as `Exact`.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Drop `plans?` from `_STAGE_SCOPE_PREFIX_RE` (making it `^(?:dev/)?proposals?\s*:\s*`), or add an explicit early return of `None` for a `dev/plans:`-prefixed subject; at minimum exclude the `plans?` branch from the `reviewed` / `revised` stages, keeping it only for `open` — the one case the justification actually argues. Add all six `dev/plans:` subjects in the corpus to the frozen regression list with expected `None`, and add `dev/plans: <slug> -- Code review (fresh-context, disclosed scribe)` with whichever classification is intended, so the choice is pinned rather than incidental. Then delete the justification sentence, since the ablation shows the branch is not required. If plan-stage and proposal-stage vocabulary are to be deliberately conflated, say so in the scope fence and state that correctness rests on first-match-wins chronological ordering. If plan-lifecycle recognition is genuinely wanted, that is new capability and must be routed to the Maintainer, not folded into a defect fix.
numbered_critiques.from_lenses: scope-stopping-rule (substantive), corpus-evidence (minor) — merged; highest severity retained

numbered_critiques.concern: The `sharpening` exclusion is NOT "carried over … unchanged" — it silently widens from a head-anchored special case into a whole-phrase suppressor, creating a new false-negative class that the proposed tests would not catch. The proposal states: "The `sharpening` exclusion is carried over from the current `reviewed` pattern unchanged — it is not part of this defect." Measured, that is false.
numbered_critiques.grounding: The shipped pattern is `^Review\b(?!.*\bsharpening\b)` (`templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/gitmeta.py:24`) — anchored, so the lookahead is only ever reachable for a subject literally beginning with "Review". The proposed pattern is `(?<!-)\breview\b(?!-)(?!.*\bsharpening\b)` applied via `.search()` over the whole stage phrase, so ANY subject containing "sharpening" anywhere after a `review` token is now suppressed. Both were exec'd and run this session on paired subjects: `dev/proposals: foo -- Internal review (fresh-context panel)` → `reviewed`, but the near-identical `dev/proposals: foo -- Internal review (fresh-context panel) + Sharpening` → `None`, and `Append Gemini External Review of foo proposal (sharpening round)` → `None`. This is not an exotic token: `git log --format="%s" | grep -ci sharpen` → 42, including three plan-review commits of exactly the vulnerable shape (`8606203`, `51f2c10`, `28816f0`, all `dev/plans: <slug> -- Plan review (fresh-context Internal) + Sharpening`). Iterating the last 400 commits, none of the 42 touches `dev/proposals/`, so live impact today is zero — but the vocabulary is in active use, so one proposal-side "Internal review … + Sharpening" subject silently drops the `reviewed` stage and downgrades the row to `Good` with no signal. Proposed test #3 asserts only `"Review sharpening pass"` → unclassified, which passes for the wrong reason and manufactures false confidence that the exclusion is unchanged.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Stop describing this as a no-op and decide it explicitly. Either scope the exclusion to the head-anchored form it actually had (e.g. apply it only when `review` leads the phrase), or drop it and state the intended behaviour. Whichever is chosen, add two tests pinning BOTH directions: `dev/proposals: <stem> -- Internal review (fresh-context panel) + Sharpening` → `reviewed` (the false-negative guard), and an implementation-style `Phase 2 (A) review Sharpening: harden facade loader` → `None` (the suppression the exclusion is presumably for). Correct the sentence in P1 so it no longer claims the exclusion is unchanged.

numbered_critiques.concern: Two independent ways the newly-populated hour deltas will be misread, both of which the proposal's own framing makes worse. (a) The repair makes `days_*` and `hours_*` openly contradict each other on 4 of 12 rows under an `Exact` label — and the proposal names that exact shape as the signal the change is WRONG, which makes its own tripwire unusable and would lead an implementer to revert a correct fix. (b) The Rationale's transparency/reproducibility claim over-reads the numbers: most newly-populated deltas measure commit batching latency, not deliberation elapsed time, and three are exactly zero — a reader will take `0.0` as a claim about review turnaround.
numbered_critiques.grounding: (a) *Signals the change is wrong* says: "a proposal reports `Exact` while an `hours_*` value contradicts the header dates in the same row. That would mean a subject matched the wrong stage — the one regression that is worse than the defect." Running `proposal_rows(Path('/Users/kendal30/Code/cairn'))` through the real `tools/_lifecycle_metrics/extract.py` with the proposed classifier patched in, and flagging rows where `days_*` and `hours_*` are both non-empty and disagree by more than a day: 4 hits — `adopter-licensing-compliance`, `first-session-survivability`, `record-corrections`, `solo-legacy-adopter-path` — each carrying `days_revised_to_decision = 11` alongside `hours_revised_to_decision ≈ 116.46` h (= 4.85 days), tier `Exact`. Cross-checked against a per-stage `(sha, timestamp, subject)` dump: the classifier is RIGHT; the header `**Date opened**` is `2026-07-11` while the actual open commit `adaa9b5` is `2026-07-17T11:55:42-04:00`, i.e. the header dates are backdated by six days. So the tripwire fires immediately on Cairn's own corpus for a reason the proposal never anticipated. Before the fix every `hours_*` was empty so the divergence was invisible; after it a third of the rows visibly disagree with themselves. (b) The proposal claims: "It also restores the sub-day resolution the tiers were designed around: post-fix, 11 of 12 proposals reach `Exact` and hour-level deltas populate." Printing every delta at HEAD `cc66d2b`: `hours_reviewed_to_revised` is exactly `0.0` for `2026-07-22-claude-interpreter-trust-root-fallback`, `…-lockfile-provenance-fields`, and `…-transition-lint`. Root cause verified in git: for interpreter-trust-root, `4f5f019` (`… -- Internal review (tailored fresh-context panel) + in-tree source`) and `841f17b` (`… -- Response + Revised (status: revised)`) both carry committer timestamp `2026-07-22T09:21:25-04:00`. Five of twelve rows also show `hours_open_to_reviewed` under 0.024 h (~85 s). These are honest readings of the commit record, but the CSV will read `0.0` next to `Exact`, and Cairn's whole pitch is that its recorded deliberation is measurable.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: (a) Rewrite the first bullet of *Signals the change is wrong* so it distinguishes backdated-header divergence (expected, benign, present on 4/12 rows today) from stage misclassification (the real regression) — e.g. key the signal on a NEGATIVE `hours_*`, or on an `hours_*` that disagrees with `days_*` in the opposite direction from the header/commit gap. Add the four rows above to the corpus test as an explicitly expected divergence with the six-day header/commit gap named, so a future implementer does not read it as breakage. (b) Replace the Rationale sentence with one that says what the numbers measure: the interval between the commits that recorded each transition, which for batch-committed sessions can be near zero. Pin the semantics rather than leaving them to be rediscovered — add at least one `0.0`-delta row (e.g. the interpreter-trust-root reviewed→revised pair) to the frozen corpus regression test with its expected value. Consider noting both the divergence and the batching semantics in the P3 docstring alongside the degradation-cause correction, since that docstring is the only adopter-facing documentation of this tier.

numbered_critiques.concern: One of the two cases offered as "Measured necessity" for the hyphen guard does not hold, and the test specified to pin the guard is non-discriminating as written.
numbered_critiques.grounding: The proposal asserts: "**Never match inside a hyphen compound** (`(?<!-)…(?!-)`). Measured necessity: without it, `dev/plans: archive review-record-integrity (Chunk C pointer + lifecycle close)` classifies as `reviewed`, and `Security-Review` inside an `open` subject does the same." Ablating the guard from both the `revised` and `reviewed` patterns and re-running over all 75 corpus subjects, exactly ONE subject flips: the `dev/plans: archive review-record-integrity …` one. `dev/proposals: open interpreter-trust-root-fallback (F2 split; Security-Review gated)` classifies as `open` with the guard AND without it — because `open` is head-anchored and first in `_STAGE_COMMIT_PATTERNS`' priority order, so the `reviewed` pattern is never evaluated for that subject. The second measured claim is false for the proposed design. The consequence reaches the test plan: Tests-required item 2 specifies asserting that same `Security-Review gated` subject → `open`, which passes identically against an unguarded pattern. It is presented as pinning the hyphen guard and does not pin it — the standing lesson "DO NOT CLAIM WHAT A TEST DOES WITHOUT READING IT" arriving one step early, a test asserted to discriminate before it exists.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Correct the sentence to name the single measured case. Keep `dev/plans: archive review-record-integrity (Chunk C pointer + lifecycle close)` → `None` as the guard's discriminating test (it is the only one in the corpus), and add a stage-phrase-position case such as `dev/proposals: interpreter-trust-root -- add Security-Review section` → `None` so the guard is pinned where the `reviewed` pattern is actually reached. Keep the `Security-Review gated` case in the suite as a priority-order test, but label it as such rather than as guard evidence.

numbered_critiques.concern: The transition-lint obligation section overstates the reuse in three specific, checkable ways, while reaching the right verdict. (a) The reuse table's row 1 is factually wrong: `_stage_for_subject` implements PRIORITY-ORDER-wins, not LEFTMOST-wins, so an implementer following the proposal's "copy three idioms that are now proven and pinned by a corpus test" would silently import the wrong disambiguation rule and violate the lint's own pinned spec. (b) The section never notes that Shape (b) — the half of the lint that actually fires on the originating incident — reads no commit message at all, so the repair contributes exactly zero to it; instead it asserts a blanket "Every finding class the lint targets is a message-versus-diff mismatch that a subject classifier is structurally blind to," which mischaracterizes Shape (b) and ironically understates the case for "still warranted." (c) "The transition-lint's own argument for not single-sourcing (its Revised prior-art subsection) survives this repair intact" is overstated — the repair falsifies one of that subsection's stated grounds outright and implements a second. The proposal applies exactly the right honesty one paragraph later to Alternative #6 ("One argument the repair partly spends"), so the inconsistency is internal to the section.
numbered_critiques.grounding: (a) Both mechanisms were implemented and compared this session. `_stage_for_subject` iterates `_STAGE_COMMIT_PATTERNS` in fixed priority order (open, decision, revised, reviewed) and returns the first pattern that matches anywhere in its target; the lint's revised spec is positional (`dev/proposals/2026-07-22-claude-transition-lint.md:1176` — "leftmost match wins, at most one claim per subject"). They diverge on 4 of 8 constructed subjects and on a real corpus subject: `dev/proposals: adopter-entry doc-refresh -- Internal review panel + Response + Revised` → `_stage_for_subject` returns `revised`; leftmost-wins returns `review`. Under the lint's claim→evidence table (`:1182-1183`) those two claims demand DIFFERENT evidence sections (`## Review` vs `## Response`|`## Revised proposal`), so the divergence is not cosmetic. (b) `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status --find-renames=100% -r 17b7e5c` → `A dev/proposals/2026-06-12-claude-check_cairn-self-host-compat.md`, so the lint's Shape (a) `open` claim IS supported by its diff and does not fire; only Shape (b) fires. Shape (b) as revised (`:1203-1206`) keys purely on the added blob's `**Status**` header and review-grammar markers (`[R<n>]`, `[E<n>]`, `**Steelman`, `**Covered**`); it parses no subject. All three rows of the reuse table are inside Shape (a). (c) The prior-art subsection's grounds are at `:1032-1042`. The ground "An anchored `^(?:Open proposal|...)` cannot express 'claims a review anywhere in the subject.'" (`:1040-1041`) is spent: post-repair the `reviewed` pattern is a `search` over the de-prefixed stage phrase, which expresses approximately that — verified, since `dev/proposals: add Gemini External Review for check_cairn self-host-compat` classifies `reviewed`. The second ground, "hyphen-compound suppression (so slugs do not read as claims)" (`:1038-1039`), is now implemented in `gitmeta.py` by the proposed `(?<!-)…(?!-)` guard. What survives is the different-question ground and the claim→evidence mapping ground — sufficient, but not "intact."
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: (a) Split row 1 of the table into what is and is not supplied: `_stage_for_subject` supplies "at most one classification per subject"; it does NOT supply leftmost-wins, which the lint must still implement. Add the one-sentence reason the two can legitimately differ — the stage reader's four stages are ordered by the lifecycle so priority order is meaningful, whereas the lint's claim tokens have no such order and must resolve positionally — and drop or qualify the "copy the idiom" framing for this row. (b) Add one sentence: the three reused idioms live entirely in Shape (a); Shape (b) — which is what fires on `17b7e5c` and is the incident that motivated the lint — consumes no subject vocabulary and is untouched by this repair. That is a sharper statement of "still warranted" than the current blanket claim, and it is verifiable. (c) Replace "survives intact" with an explicit two-column accounting: SPENT — "an anchored regex cannot express 'claims a review anywhere'" and "hyphen suppression must be invented"; SURVIVING — "different question (which commit IS stage X vs does THIS commit's claim match THIS diff)" and "claim→evidence mapping gitmeta has no concept of." The conclusion is unchanged; the argument becomes auditable.

numbered_critiques.concern: The proposal's own corpus run surfaced a NEW real false positive in the sibling lint's revised Shape (a) spec, on a commit that post-dates the sibling's pinned dogfood window, and did not report it. Feeding exactly this kind of evidence back is what the assigned obligation exists to do.
numbered_critiques.grounding: Verified this session. Commit `88fd91f`, subject `dev/proposals: transition-lint -- record Maintainer sequencing direction (not a Decision)`: `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status --find-renames=100% -r 88fd91f` → `M dev/proposals/2026-07-22-claude-transition-lint.md` (a trigger per `dev/proposals/2026-07-22-claude-transition-lint.md:1136-1138`), and the only added heading is `+## Sequencing note -- Maintainer direction -- 2026-07-22`. The lint's `decision` token is NOT positionally anchored (only `open` is — `:1181`) and matches as `(?<![-\w])decisions?(?![-\w])` per `:1176`, so the parenthesized "(not a Decision)" claims a Decision with no `## Decision` evidence → a Shape (a) finding. This commit falls outside the pinned window `d6646a3..57d1daf` (`:1299`), so the sibling's "0 false positives" row does not cover it. The repaired reader correctly returns `None` on the same subject.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Report `88fd91f` in the obligation section as measured evidence bearing on the lint's size: the lint's `decision` token likely needs the same positional anchoring `open` received, and the reader repair supplies a working precedent for that. This is a genuine, checkable contribution the section is uniquely positioned to make.

numbered_critiques.concern: Three smaller accuracy problems in the obligation section. (a) The Maintainer's obligation was "necessary, and if so at what size" (`## Sequencing note`), and the size half is answered qualitatively; the one quantitative statement — "three of the revised Shape (a) design decisions" — sizes a fraction of a fraction without naming the denominator, so the Maintainer cannot price the deferral. (b) The "design-level, not import-level" caveat rests on a ground already falsified by precedent in this repo, while a stronger ground is available and unused. (c) The section does not state that the repaired vocabulary is not a drop-in even for the message side, because it deliberately omits tokens that are load-bearing in the lint's claim table.
numbered_critiques.grounding: (a) Shape (a) as revised (`dev/proposals/2026-07-22-claude-transition-lint.md:1167-1199`) pins more than three things: case-insensitivity (`:1169-1174`), the full claim vocabulary including `accept`/`reject`/`supersede` (`:1184`), the claim→required-evidence mapping (`:1179-1184`), the ≥3-added-non-blank-line evidence rule (`:1198-1199`), and post-image section-span computation (`:204-206`). None are supplied by this repair. (b) The caveat says importing "would create a new dependency from Cairn's tooling onto a shipped template file." That precedent already exists: `scripts/check_cairn.py` loads three shipped template modules by path via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` — `templates/modules/default-on/claim_check.py`, `templates/modules/team-gated/content_scan.py`, `templates/modules/team-gated/link_check.py` (read at `scripts/check_cairn.py:83-104`). The sibling proposal already noted this and gave the real ground at `:1163`: `bootstrap/tests/_gate_manifest.py` byte-freezes `templates/modules/**/*.py` — verified in the glob list at `bootstrap/tests/_gate_manifest.py:166`. (c) The scope fence explicitly excludes `archive`, `supersede`, and implicitly `accept`/`reject`; the lint's revised claim table maps `decision` / `accept` / `reject` / `supersede` → `## Decision` (`:1184`). Verified: `dev/proposals: foo -- SUPERSEDE bar` → `None` under the proposed reader; the real corpus subject `dev/proposals: Maintainer Decision -- SUPERSEDE automated-review-committer (+ archive)` classifies `decision` only because "Decision" happens to lead.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: (a) State the denominator in one line — e.g. "3 of the ~8 pinned Shape (a) decisions, and 0 of Shape (b), the trigger/enumeration design, the exemption model, suppression, the CLI, and exit behaviour" — so the answer reads as a measurement rather than an impression. (b) Swap the ground: cite the `templates/modules/**/*.py` byte-freeze plus this proposal's own fence (`_stage_for_subject` is private and explicitly not exported) as why a repo-local script should not couple to it; the current wording invites a reviewer to point at `check_cairn.py` and dismiss the caveat. (c) Add one sentence noting the vocabulary asymmetry — the lint needs `accept`/`reject`/`supersede` as first-class claim tokens that this reader deliberately does not carry — so the Maintainer does not read "claim detection is now proven prior art" as "the lint can adopt this vocabulary."

numbered_critiques.concern: P2's fall-through removal changes nothing on the real corpus, so "This is not hypothetical" overstates its evidentiary basis. The proposal introduces P2 with that phrase and cites the two `open`-classified commits in `review-record-integrity`'s history. The proposal does concede this honestly two sentences later ("P1's hyphen guard blocks that particular subject, but the fall-through is the general hazard"), so this is a framing issue rather than a false claim — but an opening "This is not hypothetical" attached to a change with zero measured effect invites a reviewer to over-credit it, and P2 ends up pinned only by the synthetic proposed test #5.
numbered_critiques.grounding: Both loop shapes were implemented this session over `gitmeta._git_log_for_path` output for all 12 proposal files, with the proposed patterns held constant: the shipped fall-through loop (`gitmeta.py:81-85`, which re-tests a subject against remaining stages when its correct slot is already filled) versus the proposed loop. The resolved `{open, reviewed, revised, decision}` SHA assignments are identical for **0 of 12**. Confirmed the specific cited case: `dev/plans: open review-record-integrity (+ archive proposal)` classifies `open` under the new patterns, and under the old loop its fall-through re-test yields no match for `decision`/`revised`/`reviewed` because the hyphen guard blocks `review-record`.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Keep P2 — it is cheap, correct, and makes classification a pure function of the subject, which is the right invariant. But retitle the justification honestly: say the fall-through is a latent defect of the same mechanism with no currently-observable effect (measured 0/12), rather than "not hypothetical". Keep proposed test #5 and note in the test docstring that it is the only thing pinning P2, since the live corpus does not exercise it.

numbered_critiques.concern: Three presentation/measurement-accuracy defects in a proposal whose entire value proposition is measurement accuracy. (a) The de-anchored figure is 52, not the claimed 51, and Alternative 3 as literally worded produces 0, not 51. (b) The Evidence figures are stale at open time and one citation is off by one line. (c) The Context block is formatted as a verbatim shell transcript but is a hand-written summary; the command shown does not produce the output shown.
numbered_critiques.grounding: (a) Re-measuring on the exact 73-subject set as of `7d2d034` (reconstructed by removing from the 75-subject HEAD corpus the two subjects added by `cc66d2b` and `33edd10`), stripping the leading `^` from all four shipped patterns and matching with `.search()` gives **52/73**, not 51/73. Separately, *Cause 1* correctly states that switching `.match()` to `.search()` alone "would change nothing" because the `^` lives inside the pattern string — but Alternative 3 is worded "Just remove the `^` anchors", and removing the anchors while keeping the shipped `pattern.match(subject)` call at `gitmeta.py:83` yields **0/73**. The 51 (52) figure silently requires BOTH changes. Three variants run this session: shipped + `.match()` → 0/73; de-anchored + `.match()` → 0/73; de-anchored + `.search()` → 52/73. Neither error touches the conclusion — 15 of the 52 are slug-driven false positives, exactly as claimed. (b) The proposal anchors everything to "`HEAD` `7d2d034`"; actual HEAD is `cc66d2b`, two commits later (`33edd10 dev/proposals: ast-known-new-repin -- Response to Gemini Internal review`, `cc66d2b dev/plans: archive first-session-survivability (lifecycle complete)`). Re-measured: 75 distinct subjects not 73; 69 classified not 68; 6 correctly unclassified not 5 — the sixth being `dev/plans: archive first-session-survivability (lifecycle complete)`. The 0-match count and the tier table both reproduce exactly, so no conclusion moves. The proposal cites "`docs/quickstart.md:232`" for `git commit -q -m "Open proposal: README tagline"`; that line is at `docs/quickstart.md:231` and `:232` is the closing code fence. `scripts/claim_check.py` only hard-flags out-of-bounds line citations, so an in-bounds off-by-one passes silently. (c) The proposal presents a fenced block with a `$` prompt: `$ ~/conda_envs/lhm/bin/python tools/lifecycle_metrics.py proposals --format csv` followed by `12 rows; stage_timestamp_reliability = Best-effort on 12 of 12`. Running that exact command emits a CSV header plus 12 data rows and nothing resembling that summary line. The underlying fact is true (confirmed independently via `proposal_rows(Path('.'))` → `Counter({'Best-effort': 12})`), so this is presentation, not a false claim — but a `$`-prompted block that is not the command's output is the specific artifact shape this repository's review-record-integrity work exists to catch, in the one section a reader is most likely to accept without re-running.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: (a) Correct 51 → 52 in both the *Why it misses* section and Alternative 3, and reword Alternative 3 to "remove the `^` anchors and switch `.match()` to `.search()`" so the measurement is reproducible from the description; optionally note that de-anchoring alone (keeping `.match()`) still yields 0/73, which strengthens Cause 1. (b) Re-anchor the SHA and re-run the three counts immediately before the opening commit; update the five-item unclassified enumeration to six and name the archive commit; correct the quickstart citation to `docs/quickstart.md:231`. (c) Either show the real reproducer (e.g. the two-line `proposal_rows` + `Counter` snippet, which does print that fact) or drop the `$` prompt and label the block as a derived summary with the command named in prose.
numbered_critiques.from_lenses: corpus-evidence (a), scope-stopping-rule (b, c) — merged as three labelled sub-findings

numbered_critiques.concern: Three process-and-verification items. (a) The proposal asks the Maintainer three questions for what is scoped as a single defect fix, and one of them (P3) is the author's call; folding it in also requires a completeness correction the proposal does not make. (b) The declared `required(Internal)` plan-review tier is defensible on the doctrine text, but the plan should carry an explicit obligation to re-run the corpus ablation, because the density of spec-level defects here is not what "ordinary" implies. (c) The `0 Best-effort` headline is not reproducible under concurrent git load, which the smoke check and proposed test #6 should account for.
numbered_critiques.grounding: (a) Open question 2 asks "**Whether P3 rides along** or is dropped to keep the diff to one file pair." P3 is a two-line docstring correction in the same module directory, in a twin pair the author must already keep byte-identical, correcting a sentence verified factually wrong: `templates/modules/default-on/_lifecycle_metrics/__init__.py:74-78` reads "when git is absent, the path is not a checkout, or the default branch is named ``main`` rather than ``master``" — none of which describes the observed 12/12 `Best-effort`. The proposal's gate-manifest paragraph establishes that `gitmeta.py` is stale in the fixture but does not say the same of P3's file: `bootstrap/tests/fixtures/gate_manifest.json` places BOTH files in `frozen_files`, and both are stale (fixture `fb1c4d26…` for `__init__.py` vs on-disk `c0e169e7…`). The `__init__.py` twins are byte-identical (`c0e169e7…`), so the parity cost is one mechanical copy. (b) `doctrine/dual-review.md:184-187` reads "line names the tier, and that tier is chosen on the same / structural-independence axis as any other review here — an Internal-floor / read for an ordinary plan, a different-agent-type External round for a / high-risk or contract-touching one." Against `AGENTS.md`'s enumerated high-risk surfaces, `gitmeta.py` is none of them and the install contract is untouched, so Internal is the right floor. But R2, R3, R5 and R6 above were all found by EXECUTING the proposed regexes and ablating them against the real corpus, and none were visible from reading the proposal's own before/after table — which reproduces exactly and is therefore reassuring in a misleading way. (c) While the full pytest suite ran in the background, an otherwise identical pipeline run returned `2026-07-11-claude-record-corrections` as `Best-effort` — {'Exact': 10, 'Good': 1, 'Best-effort': 1} instead of the stable {'Exact': 11, 'Good': 1}; three re-runs on a quiet tree (after 1437 passed, 123.55s) were stable. consolidated.second_round_recommendation:
CONSOLIDATED RECOMMENDATION: **Author Response + Revised section, then a narrow Internal re-read with an EXECUTION obligation — not a full second panel, and not External.** All three lenses converge here.

Why not send it back to the drawing board: the diagnosis is correct, the fix is a genuine repair on Cairn's own corpus (every slot assignment across 12 proposals was hand-audited and is semantically right), the scope fence is the strongest in this tree, and the citation discipline is unusually clean. Nothing found undermines the central case that the shipped vocabulary reads nothing and should be repaired now.

WHAT GATES THE DECISION. R1 (bare-subject fallback) is blocking — not because the proposal is wrong but because it defers a decision that should be made with numbers in hand, and the panel now has the numbers. Under the standing postdoc-ready-first directive, shipping a default-on tool that labels \"Add impulse response function to the transport solver\" as a `revised` transition and reports the timestamp as `Exact` is a real regression in the adopter path: before the fix that adopter got nothing; after it they get something wrong with a confidence label attached. The proposal itself names this as the one failure mode worse than the defect, then routes it to a post-hoc tripwire. The measured trade is cheap enough to settle in one revision round — prefix-required costs exactly one tier on Cairn's corpus and takes all 8 adopter false positives to `None`. Suggested landing: the hybrid (prefix-required plus an explicitly-enumerated `Append/Refine … Review of <stem> proposal` form), which preserves 11 `Exact` AND closes the general fallback. Whichever way the Maintainer goes, record it as a deliberate precision/recall trade in the proposal body.

Two further findings should be treated as near-blocking by one lens each and are cheap to fix in the same round: **R2** (`decision` head-anchoring returning `reviewed` on a slug-first Decision subject) is a live wrong-stage-at-`Exact` output on the corpus's own dominant subject style, and needs a code-level answer in P1 or an explicit, tested concession that decision-first is mandated; **R3** (the `plans?` prefix branch) puts a wrong-timestamp-at-`Exact` hazard into shipped default-on code in service of a branch measured to change no outcome.

The remainder resolve by appending a Response and a Revised section; none requires re-measuring anything from scratch. R4 is a corrected factual claim plus two tests. R5 matters disproportionately because as written the tripwire fires immediately on the shipped corpus, so an implementer following the proposal faithfully would revert a correct fix. R6 is a corrected sentence plus a discriminating test. R7–R9 are surgical edits confined to the obligation section (plus one additive paragraph reporting `88fd91f`); they change that section's precision, not its verdict. R10–R12 fold into the same Response: soften \"not hypothetical\" on P2, correct 51→52, reword Alternative 3 so it is reproducible, re-anchor every figure to then-current HEAD, fix the `docs/quickstart.md` off-by-one, relabel the Context block, decide P3 rather than asking, and add the quiet-tree caveat to the smoke checks.

WHAT THE SECOND READER MUST BE GIVEN: an explicit EXECUTION obligation, not a reading one. Four of the six highest-severity findings (R2, R3, R5, R6) were invisible from reading the proposal and surfaced only by executing the proposed regexes and ablating them against the live corpus. The reader must re-run the classifier over the live `git log --follow` subject set at then-current HEAD, re-run at least the `plans?`-prefix and hyphen-guard ablations, and report counts (each run takes seconds).
